assessment_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Counting and Number Patterns Activity
subject: Mathematics

sections.title: Concrete Activity: Number Line Jumps
sections.instructions: Teacher sets up a large number line on the floor from 0 to 30. Learners take turns jumping forward and backward according to teacher prompts. Each learner completes 3 jumps and records their final position.
sections.stimulus: Large floor number line (0-30) with numbered cards, teacher prompt cards (e.g., 'Jump forward 5', 'Jump back 3'), recording sheets for learners.

questions.question: Start at 0. Jump forward 4, then forward 6. Where do you land?
memo: 1 mark for showing jumps on number line or mental calculation

questions.question: Start at 20. Jump back 7, then forward 3. Where do you land?
memo: 1 mark for showing backward and forward jumps

questions.question: Show two different ways to get from 5 to 15 using jumps of 5.
memo: Accept: 5 → 10 → 15 (two jumps of 5) or 5 → 15 (one jump of 10, but note: jump size must be 5 per instruction — so only valid is two jumps of 5)
Clarify: If jump size fixed at 5, only 5→10→15 is valid. Award 2 marks for correct sequence
If learner shows 5+5+5=15 with three jumps, award 1 mark for effort but note deviation

rubric.criterion: Accuracy in number line jumps and final position
rubric.descriptor: Learner correctly performs jumps and records final position with minimal teacher support.
Learner demonstrates more than one correct method to reach a target number using given jump sizes.

rubric.criterion: Recording and communication of mathematical thinking
rubric.descriptor: Learner uses pictures, numbers, or words to clearly show their jump sequence and reasoning.
Learner actively participates, follows instructions, and takes turns appropriately during the concrete activity.

teacher_review_checklist: Assessment uses concrete activity mode as required by foundation.mathematics profile
Reading load is minimal and grade-appropriate (oral prompts, visual number line)
Teacher-facing prompts and observable learner actions are central
Mark allocation sums to 20 and aligns with rubric criteria
Memo provides clear, objective scoring guidance
No default-off modes (essay, long response, exam) are used
At least one CAPS evidence document is implied via alignment to Grade R number sense (foundational for Grade 3)
Duration (30 mins) is suitable for foundation phase activity-based assessment
Instructions are clear for both teacher and learner
Rubric criteria are observable and developmentally appropriate for Grade 3
